name: ubiquitous-language
title: A mandated ubiquitous language across the plugin family
outcome: One term means one thing across every plugin, skill, design, and ADR in the repo, and a new or colliding term cannot reach a merged pull request undetected.
abort_if: a first mechanical check of an existing term set produces mostly false positives, showing that a script cannot tell a real term from ordinary prose
design authors route around the language stage on three or more designs in a row, showing that enforcement is worked around rather than followed

min_work.derived_from: A case-insensitive grep for ubiquitous|domain-driven|bounded context|aggregate|domain event|glossary|ddd returns zero hits in plugins/cobuilder-architect/skills/architecture/references/design-mode.md and zero hits in plugins/cobuilder-implement/skills/implement/SKILL.md. plugins/cobuilder-architect/skills/architecture/references/corpus/principles/ddd/ holds 11 files, loaded by design mode's Ground stage and by review mode, but nothing checks the result. architecture-documentation.md section 3 requires a context canvas to carry a ubiquitous language of 5 to 15 terms that disambiguates homonyms shared with other contexts, and describe mode obeys it. docs/architecture/contexts/cobuilder-packaging/canvas.md section 3 defines Skill as five skills, architecture, odyssey, mermaid, ste-writing, and collaborate-with-user, and three of those five names are now wrong. Its boundary.yaml public_interface still lists commands/submit.md and commands/explore-design.md, both deleted, and scripts/_bundle_meta, which moved to shared/. The canvas also states that Skill and command carry the same meaning across the whole repo, with no homonym conflict against CLAUDE.md's vocabulary table, and that claim is now false because CLAUDE.md's table and the canvas section do not know about each other. CLAUDE.md itself records the lesson: a process step with no mechanical consumer gets skipped, however well it is documented, citing Gate 4b, which ran for zero of five multi-slice epics before it gained a mechanical check.
min_work.note: Stages 2 through 7 are deliberately deferred. This design is a backlog entry, not an approved design. It carries no intent.json, narrative.json, assessment.json, or diagrams, and it must not be implemented until design mode runs to completion.

epics.note: One language record, and it is the tracer bullet. docs/architecture/language.md becomes the single source of truth for a term, its owning context, its meaning, and what it must not be confused with. It is seeded from CLAUDE.md's existing Vocabulary table and from cobuilder-packaging's canvas section 3. shared/build_index.py projects it into the record index, so the viewer can render it. This epic is independently shippable and does not depend on E2 through E5.

Design mode gains a language stage. A design that introduces a new term must declare it or reuse an existing entry from the language record. A collision with an existing term becomes a challenge-stage finding. This fits design mode's existing no-citation-no-challenge rule, because the language record gives the challenge stage something concrete to cite.

The mechanical consumer, in cobuilder-implement. A Gate 4b technical solution design that names a concept absent from the language record fails the gate. This epic is what stops the whole program from rotting the way canvas section 3 did. E1 and E2 without E3 are documentation waiting to go stale.

A verifier that exits non-zero. A script finds a term used in a design or an ADR and absent from the language record, and fails the check. It is modeled on plugins/cobuilder-implement/scripts/verify_gate.py, which exits non-zero on any failed Gate 4 sub-step. The honest open question is that deciding what counts as a term mechanically, rather than by judgement, is the hard part of this epic and may need its own exploration.

Repair the existing drift. Refresh cobuilder-packaging's canvas section 3 and its boundary.yaml public_interface against the shipped five-plugin tree, delete the now-false homonym comment, and reconcile the two glossaries into E1's record.
